root_cause_of_round1: Round 1 decided 'keep the grid' on the ABSENCE of a bad signal rather than the PRESENCE of a good one. Both blocking findings follow from that single error.

findings.measured: CERTAIN_FAIL returns AcceptDecision(accept=False) and mutates NOTHING on the PageOutput -- status stays SUCCESS, failure_mode stays NONE, rejection_class stays empty. Every round-1 keep rule was a denylist and could not match a disposition that was never written, so a grid the value guard positively refuted shipped over a fail-closed floor.
findings.fix: manifest.D3_SUPERSEDING_REJECTIONS -- an ALLOWLIST of positively-identified soft dispositions. Empty rejection_class keeps the marker. No denylist extended.

Selection is no longer keyed on ladder position for safety. best_output wins when it qualifies (_best_effort already judged it most trustworthy -- a judgement, unlike an index); ladder order is only a tie-break when the winner was cleared, as it was in the measured run.

findings.action: tests/test_gh205_tr3_unconditional_event.py reverted to origin/main byte for byte (git checkout origin/main --). The exhaustive table_region_unverifiable pin is restored unchanged and passes (17 passed).
findings.evidence: That fixture's OCR stub produces a PageOutput with an empty rejection_class, so under the allowlist its page no longer qualifies to supersede, the D3 floor fires, and the disposition is emitted exactly once. The round-1 widening was a symptom of the round-1 defect, not a consequence of the feature.
findings.concession: The reviewer was right and my round-1 'not weakened' label was wrong: accepting either disposition IS the weakening.

findings.fix: Kept text = model reading (unedited, leading) + in-body flag note in #259's shape + the same d3_floor_png_ref the floor would have shipped. Byte-equality with model_grid_text is gone by design; tests assert containment PLUS position, that the note never matches is_page_failed_marker, and that a failed PNG render degrades to note-only exactly as the floor degraded to marker-only.

scope_extension_flagged_for_review.what: Added REJECTION_JUDGE_ONLY ('judge_only') in result.py and set it at ONE site in agentic.py -- the 'verifier found no issue, inner judge alone refused' path -- before _apply_structural_gate runs, exactly as REJECTION_AMBIGUOUS_DEFERRED is.
scope_extension_flagged_for_review.why: #260 only ever needed soft-vs-hard on the AMBIGUOUS branch, so it writes one value on one path. #262 needs the same call on every branch, and the branch the reference page most plausibly took writes nothing at all. Reading 'nothing' as soft is the round-1 bug; reading it as hard makes the fix INERT on the page it exists for.
scope_extension_flagged_for_review.unmeasurable: I cannot determine which path Cochrane-Piazzesi p15 actually took -- the issue records the flags and the cached text, not the disposition. That uncertainty is exactly why I widened the SOURCE (record the disposition) rather than the READER (loosen the allowlist).
scope_extension_flagged_for_review.safety: Still an allowlist, still fail-safe on empty. Set before the structural gate, which returns a rejecting decision unchanged and never touches the field, so a deterministic gate rejection can never be mislabelled.
scope_extension_flagged_for_review.scope_guard: flagged_model_page_output (#259) deliberately does NOT accept the new value -- its fallback is a complete native reading, so it can afford the narrower one-value list. Pinned by test_gh259_allowlist_is_not_widened_by_the_new_disposition.
